description: The main window's page may run operations of the catalog through `op`, receive change events through `subscribe`, signal their first screen, check spelling in the editor, attach files the person chooses or drops to a task or a wiki page (the page names the task or the page, never a path), open or save a copy of an attached file through the system, save an export of the list or a picture of the Gantt chart where the person chooses, export to an archive and import one that the person chooses in the native file chooser (the page names projects and a token, never a path), export a wiki page where the person chooses (the page names the page, never a path), import a folder of Markdown files into a wiki that the person chooses in the native folder chooser (the page names the project and a token, never a path), import tasks from a CSV file that the person chooses in the native file chooser (the page names the project, the mapping and a token, never a path), choose the backup folder in the native folder chooser, add a folder agents may use in the native folder chooser and take one away (the page names a folder only to take it away), read the agents' local HTTP endpoint and its token, change its port, make a new token and turn it on (after the native confirmation) or off, open a web or mail address in the desktop's browser or mail program, receive in the main window the tasks of links handed to the running app, open a task or a wiki page in its own window, read and change the app's own settings (background mode, notifications and safe rendering) and the person's time zone, switch starting with the system on and off, restart the app so that safe rendering applies, list the time zones to choose from, and keep the page's own preferences for the next start, show the quick-add window, read and change the desktop-wide quick-add shortcut, see where the command-line tool is and link the bundled one into the person's own programs folder (the page names no path), list, make, rename and open the workspaces of the data folder by name (the page names no path; opening one closes the task and wiki windows of the one before), read the licence and the third-party notices that came with the app (the page names which, never a path), quit the app (also in background mode), set their title, and move, minimize, maximize and close its own window, for the header bar. The task and wiki windows have a smaller capability of their own. Nothing else of Tauri's API is reachable from the page.
